description: A tflspec workbook: one sheet per grain. Sheets whose name starts with _ are not read (notes). Each column is described on its header cell's comment and by tfl_spec_columns().
The report a row belongs to. Blank: a study-wide default; a row naming a report replaces the default row with the same key (ARD analyses: the report the analysis serves).
A column for people, on any sheet; never read. Any other column a sheet does not read is an error (a mistyped header).
Several values in one cell: | between them.

In titles, footnotes, header and footer cells: {PAGE} {TOTAL_PAGES} {AUTO_PAGE} {AUTO_TOTAL_PAGES} (page numbers), {PROGRAM} {PROGRAM_FULL} {PROGRAM_NAME} {PROGRAM_DIR} (the program; {PROGRAM_FULL} its absolute path), {DATETIME} {DATETIME:%Y-%m-%d} (the run), the report's own: {OUTPUT_ID}, {OUTPUT_LABEL} (Table 14.1.1, made from the ID; the tokens rows OUTPUT_KIND_TABLE / _LISTING / _FIGURE change the words), {OUTPUT_TITLE} {OUTPUT_POPULATION} {OUTPUT_SECTION} {STUDY_ID} (blank unless the tokens sheet says them; a line left with nothing but them is not printed), and your own from the tokens sheet ({STUDY} ...).
What is one for the whole study: one row a key. Table / report keys: rounding, output_path, program_dir. ARD keys: id, output, source. No output_id.

The fact: rounding (r: round half to even; sas: round half away from zero; blank: options(rtfreporter.rounding)); output_path (the folder of the RTF files); program_dir (the folder of the programs, for {PROGRAM}); ARD: id (the subject key; default USUBJID), output (the study ARD's file; default output/ard/ard.rds), source (R files of the study's own analysis functions, relative to the study folder, | between them).
Its value, as text.
key / value: spec_version (a workbook of a newer version is refused by an older tflspec).
spec_version.
A whole number.
ARD: the study's data, one row a dataset.
A name for the data, used by populations and analyses (and the object's name in the program, in lower case).
SDTM or ADaM (for people and ARS; not read by the program).
Its file, relative to the study folder; the reader follows the extension: .rds, .xpt, .sas7bdat, .csv, .parquet.
New columns, NAME = R expression, | between them (transform()); blank: none.
ARD: the populations, one row a population.
The population's name, used by analyses.
The dataset its subjects come from.
An R condition on that dataset choosing the subjects; blank: every row.
Columns added to the population, NAME = R expression, | between them; blank: none.

ARD: named data the analyses read (the study's, one row a data): from a dataset or an analysis data above it, the subjects of a population, the records a condition keeps, columns of the population added, columns derived, one row per set of values. In that order. An analysis names one in `data`, or as its `denominator`.
The data's name, and its object's name in the ARD program: a lower-case letter first, then letters, digits, _ or . -- not a dataset's, pop_<population>'s or another data's.
A name a person reads; blank: none.
What it is made from: a dataset, or an analysis data of a row above.
Keeps the subjects of this population; blank: no restriction here (made from an analysis data: that one's population).

Keeps the subjects of an analysis data above (a report's own subjects: the safety set in phase 1 ...): the numerator kept to the denominator's subjects. Instead of population_id; blank: no restriction here.
An R condition on the records (the numerator's filter); blank: every record.

Columns of the population's data (its dataset, ADSL) -- or of the data of `subjects` -- added by the subject key, | between them; a column of the same name is replaced. Needs a population or subjects, here or above; blank: none.
New columns, NAME = R expression, | between them (transform()); a column the code lists list becomes a factor in their order; blank: none.
The columns kept, | between them (the subject key always); with derive, what transmute() does; blank: every column.
One row for each set of values of these columns, | between them (dplyr::distinct(), the first row kept): a denominator per subject and phase; blank: every row.

R that makes the data itself, when the columns cannot say it: its value is the data; the datasets (adae), pop_<population> and the analysis data above are in reach. With it, the columns but from are left blank; blank: the columns make the data.
ARD: one analysis a row; each becomes one cards / cardx call in the ARD program, its result tagged with output_id, analysis_id and population_id.
The analysis's id within its report; an ARD column.

The analysis this one runs inside: an analysis of the same report whose method is cards::ard_stack (several analyses on the same data and by, with the by counts and the total N), cards::ard_strata (within subgroups) or cards::ard_pairwise (each pair of groups). It takes the parent's dataset, population_id and where (and in a stack its by), so leave those blank; blank: an analysis of its own.
A name a person reads (for ARS and the GUI); blank: none.
What is computed: a keyword of tfl_ard_methods() (continuous, categorical, hierarchical ...), any pkg::function (cards::, cardx::), or a function of the study's own that the study key source loads.
The analysis data analysed (a data_id of analysis_data), instead of dataset and population_id: the population is its population; blank: dataset and population_id say it.
The data analysed; blank: the population's own dataset. Blank when `data` is given.
The population: the data is restricted to its subjects; blank: no restriction (population is NULL), or the population of `data`.
An R condition on the data, applied after the population (on an analysis data: after its own conditions); blank: every row.
Grouping variables (cards' by), | between them; blank: none.

TRUE: the analysis again without its by, over all its subjects (cards' overall rows, no group): what a table shows as its Total column (tables$total). On a cards::ard_stack row: .overall = TRUE. Blank: by groups only.
Variables the analysis is repeated within (cards' strata: a subgroup, a parameter by visit), | between them; blank: none.
The variables analysed (cards' variables), | between them.

For continuous / categorical / missing: the statistics computed, in order (tfl_ard_statistics()); for other methods: the statistics kept of what the method gives; | between them; blank: the method's default.

What percentages are of: population (hierarchical and max take it anyway), row / column / cell (cards), another population, a dataset (its records of the population's subjects), or an analysis data (as it is: one row a subject and phase gives the N of each phase); blank: the method's default.

Display formats, statistic=format, | between them; VAR:statistic=format for one variable. xx.x = one decimal (the x's count only after the point), xx.x% = a proportion as a percent, a number = decimals, pvalue = <0.001 or 3 decimals; blank: the statistic's default.

More arguments of the call, as R (data and population are bound), in any order; refused if not R. An argument a column gives (by, variables, strata, denominator, statistic) may not be given here too; blank: none.

Steps on the ARD after the call, each a call with the ARD left out, | between them: cards::add_calculated_row() (a statistic computed from others), cards::filter_ard_hierarchical() (only the rows that pass), cards::sort_ard_hierarchical(), cards::diff_ard_hierarchical(), or a function of your own that takes an ARD and gives one; blank: none.
method = custom only: the R code that gives the ARD (data and population are bound).
For CDISC ARS (tfl_ars()): PRIMARY / SECONDARY / EXPLORATORY OUTCOME MEASURE; blank: tfl_ars(purpose = ).
For CDISC ARS: SPECIFIED IN PROTOCOL / SPECIFIED IN SAP / DATA DRIVEN / REQUESTED BY REGULATORY AGENCY; blank: SPECIFIED IN SAP.
Table: one row a report. Its roles (table_plan()) and the table-wide options; a verb written in code afterwards wins.
The key spread across the columns, outermost first, | between them (table_plan(cols = )).
The keys down the rows (table_plan(rows = )); name = column renames, a quoted value is a constant heading; | between them.
Where the row label comes from (table_plan(label = )); blank: .label; NA: used to tell rows apart, not printed; NULL: not used.
cells (cells built from templates) or rows (one statistic a row, the raw values) (plan_cells(stats = )); blank: cells.

Which of the ARD's values the table prints: stat (the number, rounded here: the digits sheet, a template's {x:.1f}) or stat_fmt (the ARD's own text, as it was formatted: no digits to set; a template still combines them, {mean} ({sd})); a row may say otherwise in its template ({mean:stat_fmt}, {mean:.1f}). With stats = rows: which goes in the cell (plan_cells(value = )). Blank: stat.
What joins several column keys into a column name (plan_columns(sep = )); the columns sheet names value columns with it; blank: ____.
TRUE, FALSE, or the sort keys in order, - in front for descending (plan_sort()); blank: the data's order.
The statistic totalled across columns for a frequency order (plan_sort(stat = )).
What a cell no template could fill prints (plan_cells(na = )); blank: empty.

Which population {n} in the column header is, for a table split by page (a lab parameter): page (those with that page's data), table (the population), or both as n = page | N = table for {n} and {N}; blank: page (warns when both exist and differ). Both must be in the ARD.
The heading of a Total column (plan_total()): the ARD's overall rows, its analyses run again without their by (analyses$overall), as one more column; its {n} is the study total. Blank: none.
Where the Total column goes among the column key's values: last or first; blank: last.
Table: one row a variable (an analysis variable, a column key or the label column).
The variable's name.
What prints for its name (plan_labels()); blank: the name.
Its place among the variables (a number); blank: the data's order.
Its values in print order, | between them (plan_levels()); blank: the data's order.
Its values no record has -- a code list's value, counted 0 in every column -- show (a 0 row) or hide (plan_levels(.drop_empty = )); blank: show.
Its rows under one level of another variable: that variable, a colon, the level as the table shows it (plan_nest()); after that row, one indent deeper, its own heading dropped; blank: its own block.

A report's code lists, one row a value of a variable -- its place and what it is in the data the report's program makes (the ARD, a listing's or a figure's data): the program puts them on the columns it reads (cl_<variable>, set_levels()), each a factor in the list's order, its values the labels. A value the list does not have stops the program. Every row names its report in `output_id` (a blank one is an error: copy the rows into each report that uses them). A variable's `levels` on the variables sheet, when given, is the order in the table instead; a variable's heading is the variables sheet's `label`.
The variable (an analysis variable or a column key).
A value as the data have it.
What the value is in the data the program makes, and so what prints; blank: the value.
Its place among the variable's values (a number); blank: after the numbered ones, in the sheet's order.

Table: one row a line of a cell (plan_cells()). Rows with the same variable / context / row are one chain, tried top down. With stats = rows, a row with no template is one statistic's digits (plan_digits(.rows = )): row = the statistic as the label column prints it.
What the template is for: a variable, continuous / categorical (every variable of that kind); blank: every variable.
Only the ARD rows of this context (one variable summarised two ways); blank: any.
The row's label; blank: one row a level, labelled by the level.
An R condition on the statistics; the row is used only when it holds; blank: always.
The cell's text with {statistic:format} tokens.
Decimals of a token with no format, a comma between tokens; blank: plan_digits().
Significant digits (wins over digits); blank: none.

Table: the decimals of each statistic, written once for every analysis variable, and a variable's exceptions. A template's own format ({mean:.2f}) or a cells row's digits win; a table of stat_fmt (tables$value) is not rounded here.
Blank: every analysis variable (the rule); a variable: its exception.
The statistic, as the ARD names it (mean, sd, median, p ...).
Its decimals, a whole number (p, a percent: 1 prints 61.6).
Table: one row a report. Pages, groups, blank rows, stub; the prefix names the plan verb, the rest its argument.
Rows a page (plan_paginate_rows(max_rows = )), a whole number; blank: as_rtftables()' default.
How a page break may cut: group_safe / group_force / rows / ... (plan_paginate_rows(split = )); blank: as_rtftables()' default.
Row positions to cut before, | between them, with pages_split = rows (plan_paginate_rows(break_before = )); blank: none.
Rows of a group kept together at the foot of a page, a whole number (plan_paginate_rows(min_group_rows = )); blank: the default.
Appended to a group label continued on the next page (plan_paginate_rows(cont_label = )); quote it to keep leading spaces; blank: none.

BY pages: the column(s) whose value partitions the body first, each value a page, the row budget then applying within one (plan_paginate_rows(page_by = )); | between them; print it or hide it (columns$hide); blank: none.
With group_page = TRUE: the column whose values each start a page (plan_paginate_group(col = )); blank: the outermost row key.
How groups print (plan_row_group(mode = )): value / indent / ...; blank: the default.
TRUE, or the columns (names or positions, | between them) whose repeated values print once (plan_row_group(collapse = )); blank: none.
TRUE / FALSE: one page per value of group_col (plan_paginate_group()); blank: FALSE.
TRUE / FALSE: with group_page, FALSE leaves the group column unprinted (plan_paginate_group(keep = )); blank: TRUE.
Where blank rows go: a named rule such as between_groups, or row positions -- a blank after each, 0 before the first row, -1 after the last (0 | 5 | -1) (plan_blanks(where = )); blank: none.
TRUE / FALSE: a blank row before the first row (plan_blanks(first = )); blank: the default.
TRUE / FALSE: a blank row after the last row (plan_blanks(last = )); blank: the default.
TRUE / FALSE: blank rows count towards pages_max_rows (plan_blanks(counted = )); blank: the default.
The row-key columns folded into one stub column, | between them (plan_stub(vars = )); blank: the row keys.
The stub column's name (plan_stub(name = )); blank: the default.
Spaces a level is indented in the stub, a whole number (plan_stub(indent = )); blank: the default.
How a group's summary row shows in the stub (plan_stub(group_summary = )); blank: the default.
TRUE / FALSE: fold the stub before cell styles and sorting see the rows (plan_stub(before = )); blank: FALSE.
Value columns a column page, a whole number (plan_paginate_cols(every = )); blank: no column pages.
The columns to cut before (names or positions), | between them (plan_paginate_cols(at = )).
A separator in the column names: one column page per key before it (plan_paginate_cols(cut_by = )).
Columns printed on every column page (names or positions), | between them (plan_paginate_cols(keep = )); blank: the stub.
TRUE / FALSE: TRUE puts every column page on page 1's width scale, FALSE keeps each column's width (plan_paginate_cols(fit = )); blank: TRUE.
TRUE / FALSE: FALSE never cuts inside a spanning header cell (plan_paginate_cols(allow_span_break = )); blank: TRUE.
The order the axes nest in, outermost first: group / rows / cols, or across / down (plan_paginate_cols(order = )); | between them; blank: the default.
Table: one row a printed column, by name (the stub by stub_name, a value column by its keys joined with tables$sep); .values = every value column. Named columns win over .values.
A column name, or .values.
Relative width (a number; plan_columns(widths = )). Give one to every printed column (.values covers the value columns); blank: rtfreporter's widths.
TRUE / FALSE: a row-title column (plan_columns(row_title = )); blank: FALSE.
TRUE / FALSE: align the decimal points (plan_columns(decimal = )); blank: FALSE.
TRUE / FALSE: used, not printed (plan_hide()); blank: FALSE.
Table: one row a report; plan_style()'s arguments (auto_width goes to plan_columns()). Blank: the document's or rtfreporter's default.
The table's rules: tfl (header top and bottom, a bottom rule on the last row) or none; blank: tfl.
TRUE / FALSE: realign n (xx.x) count / percent cells to one width; blank: FALSE.
TRUE / FALSE: size each column to its widest content (plan_columns(auto_width = )); an explicit rel_width wins; blank: FALSE.
Data row height in twips (1/1440 inch); blank: from the font size.
TRUE / FALSE: TRUE exact (clipped), FALSE at least; blank: FALSE.
Column-header row height in twips; blank: row_height_twips.
Blank separator row height in twips; blank: row_height_twips.
Left cell padding in twips; blank: 0.
Right cell padding in twips; blank: 0.
Font family of the table; blank: the document's (Courier).
Font size in half-points (18 = 9 pt); blank: the document's.
Placement of the table: left / center / right; blank: left.
Vertical alignment in a cell: bottom / top / center; blank: bottom.
Cell-text markup, one of script (^{} _{} as super / subscript), relational (>= <= as symbols), all, none; blank: the document's (script).
One of detect (an all-empty data row prints as one blank row), collapse (a run of blank rows prints as one), none; blank: both detect and collapse.
The column header's rules: sides from top | bottom | left | right, or none; blank: border's.
The spanning header cells' rules: sides, or none; blank: border's.
The body rows' rules: sides, or none; blank: border's.
The first body row's rules: sides, or none; blank: border's.
The last body row's rules: sides, or none; blank: border's.
The whole column header's alignment: left / center / right (rtf_table_style()); blank: each column's.
TRUE / FALSE: the whole column header bold; blank: FALSE.
TRUE / FALSE: the whole column header italic; blank: FALSE.
The body's default alignment: left / center / right (rtf_table_style()); blank: row-title columns left, the others center.
TRUE / FALSE: the body bold by default; blank: FALSE.
TRUE / FALSE: the body italic by default; blank: FALSE.
TRUE / FALSE: the body underlined by default; blank: FALSE.
The table's width in twips (1/1440 inch); blank: the page's writable width.
The table's width as a percentage of the page width; blank: the page's writable width.
The table's width as a percentage of the writable width (inside the margins); blank: 100.
The column header text's alignment, every header row: left / center / right (plan_col_header(col_header_align = )); blank: each column's data alignment.
Table: one row a plan_cell_style(), applied in order; a report's own rows replace the default rows whole.
The columns styled, | between them (.values = every value column); blank: every column.
TRUE / FALSE: TRUE styles the column header instead of the body; blank: FALSE.
An R condition over the table's columns choosing the rows; blank: every row. Two rows with a where may not set the same look: join their conditions with |.
TRUE / FALSE; blank: unchanged.
TRUE / FALSE; blank: unchanged.
left / center / right; blank: unchanged.
Text colour, #RRGGBB; blank: unchanged.
Cell shading, #RRGGBB; blank: unchanged.
TRUE / FALSE; blank: unchanged.
Left indent of the cell text in twips (not on the header); blank: unchanged.
Table: one row a header cell (plan_col_header(header = )). A report's own cells replace the default header whole.
The header row, a whole number (1 = the top).
The columns the cell sits on: a name, .values (every value column), a position or range (3, 3:31, 3:last), or KEY = value (the columns whose key has that value); | between them.
Blank: one cell over cols; each: one cell a column; a key's name: one cell per value of that key (a spanner).

What prints; a line break is Alt+Enter or \n. Tokens: {col} {col1} {col2} (the column's keys), {n} {n1} {n2} (the population at that depth, read from the ARD), {n:sum} (the total over the cell's columns). Quote it to keep leading spaces.
left / center / right (col_cell()); blank: the default.
TRUE / FALSE; blank: FALSE.
The cell's top rule: single / double / none ... (rtf_border()); blank: the header's.
The cell's bottom rule, as border_top.
Report: one row a report; blank output_id: the study's default.
table / listing / figure / user (the report's own code leaves `content`: a data frame, rtftable pages, rtfplot figures or a list of them); blank: table.
The RTF file, relative to the study key output_path; {output_id} is the report's id; blank: {output_id}.rtf.
The program's name, joined to program_dir for {PROGRAM}; blank: the file name of the program that runs, {output_id} only when none is found.
TRUE / FALSE: each named table a section with its name in the page header (rtf_tables(auto_section = )); blank: FALSE.
left / center / right: the section label (rtf_tables(section_label_align = )); blank: left.
TRUE / FALSE: each named table's name as its last title line (rtf_tables(auto_title = )); blank: FALSE.
left / center / right: that title line (rtf_tables(title_label_align = )); blank: left.
The table's font size in half-points (18 = 9 pt) (rtf_tables(font_size_half_points = )); blank: the document's.
The titles' font size in half-points; blank: the document's.
The footnotes' font size in half-points; blank: the document's.
TRUE / FALSE: FALSE drops the running page header for this report, the study's default lines included; blank: TRUE.
TRUE / FALSE: FALSE drops the running page footer, likewise; blank: TRUE.
A word drawn diagonally behind every page (rtf_document(watermark = )); blank: none.
A figure report: the figure's width in inches (rtf_figures(width_twips = )); blank: the figure's own.
A figure report: the figure's height in inches (rtf_figures(height_twips = )); blank: the figure's own.

Where the report's ARD comes from: blank (a figure: none), its own ARD definition (the analyses rows of its output_id; a figure: own); import:<file>, an ARD made elsewhere and taken in (the file in the study's input/ard/ folder, read with tfl_read_ard()); table:<output_id>, a figure's: that table's ARD.
Report: one row a report; the page (rtf_page()) and the document's text defaults (rtf_default_format()). Blank: rtfreporter's options (landscape Letter, 0.75 in margins).
letter / legal / A4 / A3 / A5; blank: letter.
landscape / portrait; blank: landscape.
Page width in inches (wins over paper_size); blank: the paper's.
Page height in inches; blank: the paper's.
Top margin in inches; blank: 0.75.
Bottom margin in inches; blank: 0.75.
Left margin in inches; blank: 0.75.
Right margin in inches; blank: 0.75.
From the page's top edge to the running header, in inches; blank: the top margin.
From the page's bottom edge to the running footer, in inches; blank: the bottom margin.
The document's font (its font table); the study's row (blank output_id) is the company's, written once in the setup code; blank: rtfreporter's option (Courier).
The body font size in half-points (18 = 9 pt); blank: rtfreporter's option.
text (centred paragraphs) / table (a content-width one-column table); blank: text.
table (content-width, with the separator rule) / text (paragraphs); blank: table.
The title block's width: content / page / a fraction of the writable width / twips; blank: content.
The footnote block's width, as title_width; blank: content.
Cell-text markup for the whole document: script / relational / all / none; blank: script.

Report: the running page header, one row a line; the line is the key (the study's lines on blank output_id, a report's own on its rows). A line with no text is a blank line; a report's line that says (none) takes the study's line of that number out.
The line number, a whole number (1 = the top).
The text at the left; tokens work.
The text in the centre.
The text at the right.

The line number.
The text at the left.

The text at the right.
Report: the titles above the table, one row a line, as header.
The line number.

The line number.

The text in the centre.
The text at the right.
Report: tokens of your own for the header, footer, titles and footnotes, one row a token, written {NAME} there; a report's row replaces the default of the same name, (none) takes it out.
The token's name: upper case, a letter then letters, digits or _; not one of rtfreporter's own ({PAGE}, {PROGRAM}, {DATETIME} ...).
What it becomes; (none) takes a default out for this report.
Listing: one row a listing (listing_spec()).
An rtfreporter listing type (listing_spec(type = )); blank: multiline.
The dataset listed (of the ARD spec's datasets catalog).
An R condition on its columns choosing the rows; blank: every row.
The sort variables, | between them, - in front for descending; blank: the data's order.
Rows a page, a whole number; blank: rtfreporter's default.

The name of an R function that breaks a cell into lines (listing_spec(wrap = )); blank: the type's own rule.
Listing: one row a printed column, in order (listing_col()).
The variables stacked in the column, | between them.
The column header; \n is a line break; blank: the variables' names.
Characters a line before the cell wraps (listing_col(width = )), a whole number; blank: never wraps.
What separates the stacked variables (listing_col(sep = )); quote it to keep its spaces; blank: the type's (/).
left / center / right (listing_col(align = )); blank: the type's (left).
TRUE / FALSE: TRUE prints a value once until it changes; blank: FALSE.
